passages.text: The deacons of the church, then, should be the bishop’s eyes, moving about with discernment and investigating the actions of each person in the church to see who is about to sin, so that, having been checked by admonition from the one who presides, that person perhaps will not carry the sin through at all. They should turn back those who desert the ranks, so that those who gather do not fail to listen to the discourses, in order that by the word of truth they may be able to clear away the discouragements that from time to time fall upon the heart from both life’s misfortunes and evil associations. For if they remain fallow for a long time, they become fuel for fire. They should also find out about those who are sick in body and bring them to the attention of the multitude that is unaware, so that its members may come forward; and they should provide what is needed according to the judgment of the one who presides. Even if they do this without his knowledge, they do not sin. The deacons, then, should take thought for these and similar matters.

lexical_decisions.chosen: should be the bishop’s eyes, moving about with discernment
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both the image of the deacons as eyes and their prudent movement throughout the community.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἑκάστου τῆς ἐκκλησίας πολυπραγμονοῦντες τὰς πράξεις τίς μέλλει ἁμαρτάνειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: investigating the actions of each person in the church to see who is about to sin
lexical_decisions.rationale: Makes τίς clearly interrogative and presents the inquiry as the purpose of examining each person’s conduct.

lexical_decisions.chosen: having been checked by admonition
lexical_decisions.rationale: Καταλαμβάνω here describes intervention reaching or arresting the person before the contemplated sin is completed.

lexical_decisions.chosen: They should turn back those who desert the ranks
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the military image of leaving one’s assigned position and the restorative force of ἐπιστρέφω.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ μὴ ἐπιλείπειν τοὺς συνερχομένους τῶν λόγων ἐπακούειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: so that those who gather do not fail to listen to the discourses
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes τοὺς συνερχομένους as the accusative subject and ἐπακούειν as the infinitival complement of ἐπιλείπειν, a defensible construction that fits the concern about continued attendance and instruction.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰς ἑκάστοτε τῇ καρδίᾳ προσπιπτούσας ἀθυμίας
lexical_decisions.chosen: the discouragements that from time to time fall upon the heart
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the source’s image of recurring discouragements falling upon the heart.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: χρόνῳ πολλῷ χερσεύσωσιν, πυρὸς ἔργον γίνονται
lexical_decisions.chosen: remain fallow for a long time, they become fuel for fire
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the movement from agricultural neglect to the image of material consumed by fire.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοὺς δὲ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα νοσοῦντας μανθανέτωσαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: They should also find out about those who are sick in body
lexical_decisions.rationale: Renders μανθάνω as ascertaining the condition of people whose illness is explicitly bodily.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται
lexical_decisions.chosen: bring them to the attention of the multitude that is unaware, so that its members may come forward
lexical_decisions.rationale: Understands the deacons as making the sick known to the congregation so that members of the collective multitude may appear or come forward; alternative referents remain possible.

source_issues.source_quote: τοῦ μὴ ἐπιλείπειν τοὺς συνερχομένους τῶν λόγων ἐπακούειν
source_issues.issue: The main rendering treats τοὺς συνερχομένους as the accusative subject of ἐπιλείπειν and takes ἐπακούειν as its complement. Other defensible attachments are possible: ἐπακούειν may describe the purpose for which people assemble, with ἐπιλείπειν meaning that they fall away or become wanting; or the deacons may be the unexpressed subject of transitive ἐπιλείπειν, yielding “so that they do not abandon those who assemble to listen.” The selected construction is contextually coherent and does not require emending the supplied Greek.

source_issues.source_quote: συνπτώσεων
source_issues.issue: The supplied edition prints the unassimilated spelling συνπτώσεων. The form is intelligible as the word conventionally normalized συμπτώσεων and does not obstruct translation.

source_issues.source_quote: ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἂν χρόνῳ πολλῷ χερσεύσωσιν, πυρὸς ἔργον γίνονται
source_issues.issue: The plural subject is not restated. The main rendering refers it to the people whose continued gathering and listening have just been discussed, which suits the image of people becoming uncultivated through neglect. A grammatical reference to the discouragements is less contextually natural but cannot be excluded solely by morphology.

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται
source_issues.issue: The rare προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν and the subject of ἐπιφαίνωνται allow more than one interpretation. The main text understands the sick as being brought to the congregation’s attention and the members of the collective multitude as then coming forward. Alternatively, the sick themselves may be the grammatical subject of “appear” or “present themselves.” The context supports the selected construction, but the Greek does not explicitly say “visit the sick.”

passages.text: The passengers, then, should remain stable, seated firmly in their own places, so that through disorder they do not cause rocking or a list to one side. The ship’s recruiting officers should remind them of the wages. The deacons should neglect none of the things entrusted to them. The elders, like sailors, should carefully prepare what each person needs. The bishop, as a watchful bow officer, should repeat only the helmsman’s words. The Messiah should be loved as Savior and helmsman, and he alone should be trusted concerning what he says. All should pray to God that they may sail with a favorable wind. Those sailing should expect every affliction, as they sail beside a great and turbulent deep—the world—at one time discouraged, persecuted, scattered, hungry, thirsty, without clothing, and distressed, and again at another time united, gathered together, and at rest, but also seasick, dizzy, and vomiting (that is, confessing offenses as though they were disease-producing bile—I mean sins arising from bitterness and the evils heaped up from disorderly desires. By confessing these, as though you had vomited them, you are relieved of the illness and receive the saving health that comes from attentive care).

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εὐσταθείτωσαν οὖν οἱ ἐπιβάται ἑδραῖοι ἐπὶ τῶν ἰδίων καθεζόμενοι τόπων
lexical_decisions.chosen: The passengers, then, should remain stable, seated firmly in their own places
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both the demand for stability and the passengers’ firm occupation of their respective places.

lexical_decisions.chosen: rocking or a list to one side
lexical_decisions.rationale: Distinguishes general shaking from an unequal inclination of the ship toward one side.

lexical_decisions.chosen: The ship’s recruiting officers should remind them of the wages
lexical_decisions.rationale: Ναυστολόγοι denotes those who enroll or recruit a ship’s company; the recipient of the reminder is implicit, while μισθοί retains the image of promised wages or rewards.

lexical_decisions.chosen: should carefully prepare what each person needs
lexical_decisions.rationale: Treats τὰ χρῄζοντα as the necessary provisions or arrangements appropriate to each person.

lexical_decisions.chosen: as a watchful bow officer
lexical_decisions.rationale: Πρωρεύς is the officer stationed toward the bow, while ἐγρηγορώς emphasizes continued watchfulness.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ κυβερνήτου μόνου τοὺς λόγους ἀντιβαλλέτω
lexical_decisions.chosen: should repeat only the helmsman’s words
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes the helmsman’s words as the direct object and understands ἀντιβάλλω as giving them back or reproducing them, fitting the bishop’s subordinate role in the ship analogy.

lexical_decisions.chosen: The Messiah should be loved as Savior and helmsman
lexical_decisions.rationale: Renders the independent title χριστός as “Messiah” and preserves both adjacent designations, σωτήρ and κυβερνήτης.

lexical_decisions.chosen: seasick, dizzy, and vomiting
lexical_decisions.rationale: The author’s ensuing explanation in terms of expelling disease-producing bile strongly supports a purgative or vomiting sense for the uncommon final form.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: προσιέμενοι τὴν ἐκ τῆς ἐπιμελείας σωτήριον ὑγείαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: receive the saving health that comes from attentive care
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the medical image of accepting restorative health produced by care or treatment.

source_issues.source_quote: ὥσπερ ’ναῦται
source_issues.issue: The supplied print places a raised mark before ναῦται although ordinary elision does not account for it. The translation treats the mark as a nonlexical editorial or typographic feature without claiming that it is an OCR error.

source_issues.source_quote: ὡς πρωρεὺς ’ἐγρηγορὼς
source_issues.issue: The raised mark before ἐγρηγορὼς is not required by the apparent syntax or ordinary elision. Its typographic or editorial function is uncertain, but it does not prevent a defensible translation of the surrounding words.

source_issues.source_quote: τοῦ κυβερνήτου μόνου τοὺς λόγους ἀντιβαλλέτω
source_issues.issue: The exact action of ἀντιβαλλέτω is lexically open. The main text chooses “repeat,” taking the helmsman’s words as what the bow officer gives back or reproduces. “Answer with” or “exchange” has support from conversational usage, while “relay” would fit the nautical setting but adds an unexpressed onward recipient. The selected rendering is defensible without altering the Greek.

source_issues.source_quote: ὁ χριστὸς ὡς σωτὴρ κυβερνήτης φιλείσθω
source_issues.issue: The single ὡς introduces the adjacent nouns σωτήρ and κυβερνήτης without an expressed conjunction. The translation coordinates them in idiomatic English as “Savior and helmsman.” They may alternatively be heard as a combined designation, “Savior-helmsman,” or as “the saving helmsman.”

source_issues.source_quote: ἐνούμενοι
source_issues.issue: The supplied form has smooth breathing. The context contrasts scattering with being united and supports identification with the unity verb conventionally written ἑνόω. This is an intelligible orthographic feature, not grounds for treating the verified print as unreadable.

source_issues.source_quote: ἀπερῶντες
source_issues.issue: The form is uncommon, but its purgative sense is made intelligible by the author’s immediate explanation involving disease-producing bile and the related form ἀπεράσαντες later in the same sentence. The exact lexical formation remains uncertain, while the contextual action is defensibly rendered as vomiting.

passages.text: Nevertheless, all of you know that the bishop toils more than all of you, because each of you suffers his own affliction, whereas he suffers both his own and that of each person. Therefore, Clement, preside as a helper to each person, as far as you are able, burdened with the cares of everyone. Accordingly, in your undertaking to administer, I know that I have received a favor, not given one. But take courage and bear it nobly, knowing that when you have reached the harbor of rest, God will give you in return the greatest of good things—an inalienable reward—because you undertook the greater toil for the salvation of all. Thus, if many of the brothers hate you because of righteousness carried to the utmost, their hatred will do you no harm, but the friendship of the righteous God will benefit you greatly. Therefore, strive to shake off praise arising from injustice, but through just administration to hunt for the beneficial praise that comes from the Messiah.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πάντων ὑμῶν πλεῖον κάμνοντα τὸν ἐπίσκοπον
lexical_decisions.chosen: the bishop toils more than all of you
lexical_decisions.rationale: The accusative-infinitive construction presents the bishop as bearing greater wearisome labor than every individual hearer.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἕκαστος ὑμῶν τὴν αὐτοῦ θλίψιν πάσχει, αὐτὸς δὲ τὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν ἑκάστου
lexical_decisions.chosen: each of you suffers his own affliction, whereas he suffers both his own and that of each person
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the contrast between each member’s individual distress and the bishop’s additional burden for every member.

lexical_decisions.chosen: preside as a helper
lexical_decisions.rationale: Combines Clement’s leading position with the explicitly stated role of helping those under his care.

lexical_decisions.chosen: burdened with the cares of everyone
lexical_decisions.rationale: The passive participle portrays Clement as loaded with the collective concerns of the community.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in your undertaking to administer
lexical_decisions.rationale: Treats σέ as the accusative subject of the whole infinitival expression: Clement undertakes the administration just assigned to him. This accords with the immediate commission and does not force σέ to be the object of οἰκονομεῖν.

lexical_decisions.chosen: an inalienable reward
lexical_decisions.rationale: The adjective describes a reward that cannot be removed or taken away.

lexical_decisions.chosen: righteousness carried to the utmost
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the expression’s image of righteousness reaching its furthest extent.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸν ἐκ χριστοῦ ἐπωφελῆ θηρεύειν ἔπαινον
lexical_decisions.chosen: to hunt for the beneficial praise that comes from the Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the hunting image of θηρεύω, the advantageous character of the praise, and Χριστός as an independent title.

source_issues.source_quote: τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι χάριν οἶδα εἰληφώς, οὐ δεδωκώς
source_issues.issue: The main rendering treats σέ as the accusative subject of the entire infinitival expression, “your undertaking to administer,” while the nominative participles εἰληφώς and δεδωκώς refer to the first-person speaker, who knows himself to have received rather than given a favor. An alternative analysis makes τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν the object of ἀναδέξασθαι, with the speaker undertaking the arrangement that Clement administer. A less contextually suitable reading takes σέ as the direct object of οἰκονομεῖν, so that the speaker undertakes to administer Clement. The explicit accusative can defensibly be the embedded subject, and the immediate commission to Clement supports that choice; no emendation is required.

source_issues.source_quote: ’σωτηρίας
source_issues.issue: The supplied print places a raised mark before σωτηρίας although no ordinary elision is apparent. The mark does not affect the intelligible phrase ὑπὲρ τῆς τῶν πάντων σωτηρίας and is treated as a nonlexical editorial or typographic feature.

passages.text: But you should also understand some things on your own, because he is unable to speak openly on account of the plots. For example, if he is hostile to someone, do not wait for him to say, “Do not have dealings with this person.” Instead, prudently follow his intention, becoming enemies of those to whom he is hostile and not associating with those with whom he does not associate, so that each person, laying claim to having everyone as friends, may be saved by reconciling him and heeding his discourse. But if anyone remains a friend of those to whom he is hostile and speaks with those with whom he does not associate, that person too is one of those who want to destroy the church. For although he is with you in body, since he is not with you in purpose, he is against you—much worse than the enemies who are visibly outside, scattering those inside while maintaining seeming friendship.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἔνια δὲ καὶ ἀφ᾽ ἑαυτῶν νοεῖν ὀφείλετε
lexical_decisions.chosen: you should also understand some things on your own
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the demand that the hearers infer matters for themselves rather than waiting for an explicit public statement.

lexical_decisions.chosen: speak openly
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase refers to public or unconcealed speech, contrasted with intentions that must be inferred because of plots.

lexical_decisions.chosen: have dealings with
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb can denote engaging, associating, or contending with someone; the surrounding language of friendship and conversation supports the broad relational rendering.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀλλὰ φρονίμως ἕπεσθε αὐτοῦ τῷ βουλήματι
lexical_decisions.chosen: Instead, prudently follow his intention
lexical_decisions.rationale: The hearers are told to discern and conform to the leader’s will even when he cannot state it openly.

lexical_decisions.chosen: laying claim to having everyone as friends
lexical_decisions.rationale: The middle verb presents the person as asserting or pursuing a claim to the state expressed by the genitive infinitival phrase.

lexical_decisions.chosen: reconciling him
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves αὐτόν as the explicit direct object of the active participle rather than silently changing the construction into self-reconciliation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: heeding his discourse
lexical_decisions.rationale: The recurring singular pronouns most naturally continue to refer to the presiding leader whose intention and associations govern the paragraph.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῇ γνώμῃ μὴ ὢν μεθ᾽ ὑμῶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: since he is not with you in purpose
lexical_decisions.rationale: Contrasts bodily presence with inward judgment, intention, or allegiance.

lexical_decisions.chosen: while maintaining seeming friendship
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the characterization of the friendship as apparent rather than genuine.

source_issues.source_quote: ἵνα ἕκαστος, ἐπιδικαζόμενος τοῦ πάντας φίλους ἔχειν, αὐτὸν διαλλάττων σώζηται
source_issues.issue: The main rendering understands ἕκαστος as each person who has become isolated through hostility toward the leader, and αὐτόν as the leader: wishing to retain everyone as friends, that person reconciles the leader and is saved. This follows the paragraph’s repeated singular reference to the leader and explains the communal withdrawal as pressure toward reconciliation. Grammatically, active διαλλάττων makes αὐτόν the affected object but leaves the other party to the reconciliation unexpressed. “Winning him back” or “effecting reconciliation with him” are viable contextual formulations, while identifying αὐτόν as a different alienated person is less contextually natural. The selected construction is defensible without supplying a named referent in the text.

source_issues.source_quote: τῆς αὐτοῦ ἐπακούων ὁμιλίας
source_issues.issue: The main text takes αὐτοῦ as the presiding leader, continuing the repeated references to his intention, hostility, and associations. It could grammatically resume another referent assigned to the preceding αὐτόν, but the leader remains the most continuous and contextually relevant antecedent. The English retains the pronoun rather than replacing it with an explicit name or office.

passages.text: After saying these things, there in the midst before everyone, he laid his hands on me and entreated me to sit in his own chair. When I had sat down, he immediately said this to me: “Before all my brothers who are present with me, I ask you that, whenever I depart from the life here (as is owed to me), you write a concise account and send it to James, the Lord’s brother, reaching even as far back as your thoughts from childhood and telling how, from the beginning until now, you have traveled with me, heeding the words and deeds proclaimed by me city by city. Then, toward the end, do not hesitate also to disclose the cause of my death, as I said beforehand. For this will not grieve him greatly, since he knows that what I inevitably had to suffer I discharged devoutly. Rather, he will obtain the greatest consolation when he learns that after me no unlearned man—ignorant of life-giving words and the church’s rule and without knowledge—was entrusted with the teacher’s chair. For discourse that leads astray destroys the souls of the crowds who hear it.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: there in the midst before everyone
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both the public location in the assembly’s midst and the presence of all as witnesses.

lexical_decisions.chosen: entreated me to sit
lexical_decisions.rationale: Construes the infinitive with the following finite verb despite the printed period, yielding the natural sense of earnestly urging Clement to take the chair.

lexical_decisions.chosen: I ask you
lexical_decisions.rationale: Introduces a formal request made before the assembled brothers.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ἀναγραψάμενον
lexical_decisions.chosen: you write a concise account and send it to James, the Lord’s brother
lexical_decisions.rationale: Treats the resumed σέ as the accusative subject of διαπέμψαι and ἀναγραψάμενον. English supplies “account” and “it” from the act of writing in epitome because διαπέμπω otherwise lacks an expressed object.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μέχρι καὶ τῶν ἐκ παίδων σου λογισμῶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: reaching even as far back as your thoughts from childhood
lexical_decisions.rationale: Presents the requested record as extending to Clement’s earliest stated thoughts or reflections.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῶν κατὰ πόλιν ὑπ᾽ ἐμοῦ κηρυχθέντων λόγων τε καὶ πράξεων
lexical_decisions.chosen: the words and deeds proclaimed by me city by city
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the unusual coordination in which κηρυχθέντων grammatically characterizes both the words and the deeds.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the cause of my death
lexical_decisions.rationale: Πρόφασις can denote cause, occasion, or pretext; an account of Peter’s death supports “cause” here.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὃ πάντως ἔδει με παθεῖν εὐσεβῶς ἀπεδόμην
lexical_decisions.chosen: what I inevitably had to suffer I discharged devoutly
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the necessary suffering as an obligation that the speaker has paid or fulfilled in a devout manner.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐκ ἀμαθὴς ἀνὴρ καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς τὴν τοῦ διδάσκοντος ἐπιστεύθη καθέδραν
lexical_decisions.chosen: no unlearned man—ignorant of life-giving words and the church’s rule and without knowledge—was entrusted with the teacher’s chair
lexical_decisions.rationale: Gives the first οὐκ broad scope over the entrusting of the described kind of successor, while rendering the further explicit οὐκ εἰδώς as “without knowledge.” This yields the consolation required by the context and preserves both negations.

lexical_decisions.chosen: For discourse that leads astray
lexical_decisions.rationale: Renders πλάνος by its active force of causing hearers to wander or be deceived.

source_issues.source_quote: καθεσθῆναί με. ἐδυσώπησεν
source_issues.issue: The printed period separates the infinitive from the finite verb that most naturally governs it. The translation construes them together as “entreated me to sit.” This treats the punctuation as an editorial feature of the supplied edition, not as proof that the Greek words are corrupt.

source_issues.source_quote: συνπαρόντων
source_issues.issue: The supplied edition prints the unassimilated spelling συνπαρόντων. It is intelligible as the form conventionally normalized συμπαρόντων and does not impede translation.

source_issues.source_quote: Ἀξιῶ σε ἐπὶ πάντων μου τῶν συνπαρόντων ἀδελφῶν, ὅπως ὁπόταν τοῦ ἐνταῦθα (ὡς ἐμοὶ ὀφείλεται) ἀπαλλάξω βίου, σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ἀναγραψάμενον
source_issues.issue: The main construction takes the second σέ as a resumed accusative subject after the intervening temporal clause, with ἀναγραψάμενον agreeing with Clement and διαπέμψαι denoting his dispatch of the resulting account to James. The following section’s statement that Clement made and sent the epitome supports this role assignment. Alternatively, σέ could formally be taken as the object of διαπέμψαι, “send you,” but that would require the speaker to remain the unexpressed subject and fits the ensuing account less well. The object sent is unexpressed in Greek and is supplied in English from the writing of the epitome.

source_issues.source_quote: ἔπειτα πρὸς τῷ τέλει καὶ τὴν τοῦ θανάτου μου πρόφασιν ὡς προεῖπον δηλῶσαι μὴ ὀκνήσῃς
source_issues.issue: The main text takes the final μὴ ὀκνήσῃς directly with δηλῶσαι: after the earlier request to write and send the account, Clement is specifically told not to hesitate to disclose the cause of the death near its end. It is also possible to give “do not hesitate” wider scope over both the dispatch and the final disclosure. The selected narrower attachment follows the immediate position of δηλῶσαι and yields a defensible sequence of instructions.

source_issues.source_quote: οὐκ ἀμαθὴς ἀνὴρ καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς τὴν τοῦ διδάσκοντος ἐπιστεύθη καθέδραν
source_issues.issue: The first οὐκ can be read with broad propositional scope: it was not a man characterized as unlearned and ignorant who was entrusted with the chair. This is the main rendering and coheres with James’s resulting consolation. A strictly local reading produces “a not-unlearned man” who nevertheless is ignorant of life-giving words and the church’s rule, an awkward contrast. Another possible analysis distributes the first negation over the coordinated descriptions, yielding the positive sense that the successor was neither unlearned nor ignorant. The explicit second negation in οὐκ εἰδώς is retained as “without knowledge.” The ambiguity concerns scope, not an unreadable source.

source_issues.source_quote: κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς
source_issues.issue: The printed period interrupts the sequence of descriptions before οὐκ εἰδώς. The translation treats the participle as continuing the characterization of the man entrusted with the chair. The punctuation is preserved as a disclosed editorial feature and does not by itself establish corruption or require a conjectural reading.

findings.source_quote: πλὴν γινώσκετε πάντες πάντων ὑμῶν πλεῖον κάμνοντα τὸν ἐπίσκοπον
findings.english_quote: Nevertheless, all of you know that the bishop toils more than all of you
findings.issue: The main text chooses indicative γινώσκετε, asserting the hearers’ existing knowledge. The form also permits an imperative, asking everyone to recognize the bishop’s greater toil; that reading has substantial contextual support in this sequence of directives. The indicative is defensible, but this material difference between assertion and exhortation is not disclosed.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a note preserving the imperative alternative and explaining the contextual reason for choosing the indicative. Alternatively, provisionally render “Nevertheless, all of you should recognize that the bishop toils more than all of you,” with the indicative alternative noted. Any changed main text requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: πάντων ὑμῶν πλεῖον κάμνοντα τὸν ἐπίσκοπον
findings.english_quote: The accusative-infinitive construction presents the bishop as bearing greater wearisome labor than every individual hearer.
findings.issue: The lexical note incorrectly identifies an accusative–infinitive construction. There is no infinitive here: κάμνοντα is an accusative participle agreeing with τὸν ἐπίσκοπον. This does not invalidate the English main text, but it makes the supporting grammatical explanation inaccurate.
findings.suggested_revision: Correct the note to describe γινώσκετε with the accusative τὸν ἐπίσκοπον and its supplementary or predicative participle κάμνοντα. Preserve the comparison expressed by πάντων ὑμῶν πλεῖον without claiming an infinitival construction.

findings.source_quote: καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς
findings.english_quote: ignorant of life-giving words and the church’s rule and without knowledge
findings.issue: The draft makes both ζωοποιοὺς λόγους and ἐκκλησίας κανόνα objects of ἀγνοῶν, then takes οὐκ εἰδώς absolutely as “without knowledge.” That construction is defensible, but the notes omit the more straightforward alternative attachment: ζωοποιοὺς λόγους belongs to ἀγνοῶν, while ἐκκλησίας κανόνα belongs to οὐκ εἰδώς. The existing discussion of negation scope does not disclose this separate object-attachment question. The alternative also preserves the source’s distinct formulations for ignorance more transparently. This is interpretive uncertainty, not evidence of source corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Add the alternative “ignorant of life-giving words and not knowing the church’s rule” and explain why the main text instead groups both objects under ἀγνοῶν and leaves οὐκ εἰδώς absolute. Explicitly compare that source-transparent alternative with the current wording. If adopting it, a provisional full formulation is “when he learns that after me it was not an unlearned man—ignorant of life-giving words and not knowing the church’s rule—who was entrusted with the teacher’s chair.” Retain disclosure of the printed period and the existing negation-scope alternatives; the proposed replacement requires fresh review.

context.title: Pseudo-Clementine Letter of Clement to James

passages.source_text: οἱ μὲν οὖν τῆς ἐκκλησίας διάκονοι τοῦ ἐπισκόπου συνετῶς ῥεμβόμενοι ἔστωσαν ὀφθαλμοί, ἑκάστου τῆς ἐκκλησίας πολυπραγμονοῦντες τὰς πράξεις τίς μέλλει ἁμαρτάνειν, ἵνα νουθεσίᾳ καταληφθεὶς ὑπὸ τοῦ προκαθεζομένου τάχα οὐ μὴ τελέσῃ τὸ ἁμάρτημα· τοὺς λειποτάκτας ἐπιστρεφέτωσαν, τοῦ μὴ ἐπιλείπειν τοὺς συνερχομένους τῶν λόγων ἐπακούειν, ὅπως τὰς ἑκάστοτε τῇ καρδίᾳ προσπιπτούσας ἀθυμίας ἔκ τε βιωτικῶν συνπτώσεων καὶ ὁμιλιῶν κακῶν λόγῳ ἀληθείας καθαίρεσθαι δύνωνται· ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἂν χρόνῳ πολλῷ χερσεύσωσιν, πυρὸς ἔργον γίνονται. τοὺς δὲ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα νοσοῦντας μανθανέτωσαν καὶ τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται, καὶ τὰ δέοντα ἐπὶ τῇ τοῦ προκαθεζομένου γνώμῃ παρεχέτωσαν· τοῦτο δὲ κἂν λάθρα αὐτοῦ ποιῶσιν, οὐχ ἁμαρτάνουσιν. ταῦτα μὲν οὖν καὶ τὰ τούτοις ὅμοια οἱ διάκονοι προνοείτωσαν.

εὐσταθείτωσαν οὖν οἱ ἐπιβάται ἑδραῖοι ἐπὶ τῶν ἰδίων καθεζόμενοι τόπων, ἵνα μὴ τῇ ἀταξίᾳ σεισμὸν ἢ ἑτεροκλινίαν παρέχωσιν. οἱ ναυστολόγοι τοὺς μισθοὺς ὑπομιμνησκέτωσαν. οἱ διάκονοι μηδὲν ἀμελείτωσαν ὧν ἐπιστεύθησαν. οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ὥσπερ ’ναῦται καταρτιζέτωσαν ἐπιμελῶς τὰ χρῄζοντα ἑκάστῳ. ὁ ἐπίσκοπος ὡς πρωρεὺς ’ἐγρηγορὼς τοῦ κυβερνήτου μόνου τοὺς λόγους ἀντιβαλλέτω. ὁ χριστὸς ὡς σωτὴρ κυβερνήτης φιλείσθω καὶ μόνος περὶ ὧν λέγει πιστευέσθω. οἱ δὲ πάντες τῷ θεῷ περὶ τοῦ οὐρίᾳ πλέειν προσευχέσθωσαν. οἱ πλέοντες πᾶσαν θλίψιν προσδοκάτωσαν ὡς μέγαν καὶ ταραχώδη βυθὸν παραπλέοντες, τὸν κόσμον· ὁτὲ μὲν ἀθυμοῦντες, διωκόμενοι, σκορπιζόμενοι, πεινῶντες, διψῶντες, γυμνητεύοντες, στενοχωρούμενοι, καὶ πάλιν ὁτὲ μὲν ἐνούμενοι, συναλιζόμενοι, ἡσυχάζοντες· ἀλλὰ καὶ ναυτιῶντες, ἰλιγγιῶντες, ἀπερῶντες (τουτέστιν ἐξομολογούμενοι τὰ παραπτώματα ὥσπερ νοσοποιοὺς χολάς, τὰς ἐκ πικρίας ἁμαρτίας λέγω καὶ τὰ ἐξ ἐπιθυμιῶν ἀτάκτων σωρευθέντα κακά, ἅτινα τῷ ὁμολογῆσαι ὥσπερ ἀπεράσαντες κουφίζεσθε τῆς νόσου, προσιέμενοι τὴν ἐκ τῆς ἐπιμελείας σωτήριον ὑγείαν).

πλὴν γινώσκετε πάντες πάντων ὑμῶν πλεῖον κάμνοντα τὸν ἐπίσκοπον, ὅτι ἕκαστος ὑμῶν τὴν αὐτοῦ θλίψιν πάσχει, αὐτὸς δὲ τὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν ἑκάστου. διό, ὦ Κλήμης, ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὸ δυνατὸν προκαθέσθητι βοηθός, τὰς πάντων φορτισθεὶς φροντίδας. ὅθεν τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι χάριν οἶδα εἰληφώς, οὐ δεδωκώς. ἀλλὰ θάρρει καὶ γενναίως φέρε ὡς εἰδὼς ὅτι ἀποδώσει σοι ὁ θεὸς εἰς τὸν λιμένα τῆς ἀναπαύσεως καταντήσαντι τὸ μέγιστον τῶν ἀγαθῶν, ἀναφαίρετον μισθόν, καθότι ὑπὲρ τῆς τῶν πάντων ’σωτηρίας τὸν μείζονα ἀνεδέξω κάματον. ὥστε ἐάν σε πολλοὶ τῶν ἀδελφῶν διὰ τὴν ἐπ’ ἄκρον δικαιοσύνην μισήσωσιν, τὸ αὐτῶν μὲν μῖσος οὐδέν σε βλάψει, ἡ δὲ τοῦ δικαίου θεοῦ φιλία πολύ σε ὀνήσει. ὥστε πειρῶ τὸν ἐξ ἀδικίας γινόμενον ἔπαινον ἀποσείεσθαι, διὰ δὲ δικαίαν διοίκησιν τὸν ἐκ χριστοῦ ἐπωφελῆ θηρεύειν ἔπαινον.

ἔνια δὲ καὶ ἀφ᾽ ἑαυτῶν νοεῖν ὀφείλετε διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν μὴ δύνασθαι ἐν φανερῷ λέγειν διὰ τὰς ἐπιβουλάς, οἷον ἐὰν ἐχθραίνῃ τινί, μὴ ἀναμένετε αὐτὸν εἰπεῖν τῷδε μὴ προσαμιλλᾶσθαι, ἀλλὰ φρονίμως ἕπεσθε αὐτοῦ τῷ βουλήματι, ἐχθροὶ γινόμενοι οἷς ἐχθραίνει καὶ μὴ ὁμιλοῦντες οἷς μὴ ὁμιλεῖ· ἵνα ἕκαστος, ἐπιδικαζόμενος τοῦ πάντας φίλους ἔχειν, αὐτὸν διαλλάττων σώζηται, τῆς αὐτοῦ ἐπακούων ὁμιλίας. εἰ δέ τις φίλος μένει οἷς αὐτὸς ἐχθραίνει, καὶ λαλεῖ οἷς αὐτὸς οὐχ ὁμιλεῖ, εἷς ἐστὶν καὶ αὐτὸς τῶν ὀλοθρεύειν θελόντων τὴν ἐκκλησίαν· τῷ γὰρ σώματι συνὼν ὑμῖν, τῇ γνώμῃ μὴ ὢν μεθ᾽ ὑμῶν, καθ᾽ ὑμῶν ἐστίν, πολλῷ χείρων τῶν ἔξωθεν φαινομένων ἐχθρῶν, μετὰ δοκούσης φιλίας σκορπίζων τοὺς ἔσω.

καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἐν μέσῳ ἐπὶ πάντων μοι τὰς χεῖρας ἐπιθεὶς εἰς τὴν αὐτοῦ καθέδραν καθεσθῆναί με. ἐδυσώπησεν. καθεσθέντι δὲ τοῦτό μοι εὐθέως ἔφη Ἀξιῶ σε ἐπὶ πάντων μου τῶν συνπαρόντων ἀδελφῶν, ὅπως ὁπόταν τοῦ ἐνταῦθα (ὡς ἐμοὶ ὀφείλεται) ἀπαλλάξω βίου, σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ἀναγραψάμενον μέχρι καὶ τῶν ἐκ παίδων σου λογισμῶν καὶ ὡς ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς μέχρι τοῦ νῦν συνώδευσάς μοι, ἐπακούων τῶν κατὰ πόλιν ὑπ᾽ ἐμοῦ κηρυχθέντων λόγων τε καὶ πράξεων, ἔπειτα πρὸς τῷ τέλει καὶ τὴν τοῦ θανάτου μου πρόφασιν ὡς προεῖπον δηλῶσαι μὴ ὀκνήσῃς. οὔτε γὰρ λίαν αὐτὸν λυπήσει τοῦτο, εἰδότα ὅτι ὃ πάντως ἔδει με παθεῖν εὐσεβῶς ἀπεδόμην, μεγίστης δὲ παραμυθίας τεύξεται, μαθὼν ὅτι μετ᾽ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἀμαθὴς ἀνὴρ καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς τὴν τοῦ διδάσκοντος ἐπιστεύθη καθέδραν· πλάνος γὰρ ὁμιλία τῶν ἀκουόντων ὄχλων ἀναιρεῖ τὰς ψυχάς.

context.translation_policy_text:
# Translation Stance

This document states the translation commitments that guide every
decision in the People's Open Bible. Declaring them is an act of
honesty: critics can assess our output against our stated
commitments rather than guessing at hidden biases.

> **Status: first draft.** This document will be refined as the
> project matures. Input and disagreement are welcomed via GitHub
> issues.

## Theological stance

The People's Open Bible does not commit to a specific denominational
or creedal doctrinal stance. Where the source texts presuppose
theological claims — the divinity of Christ, the resurrection,
the personhood of the Holy Spirit, the unity of God — the
translation reflects those claims as the texts present them, not
as imposed commitments of the translator.

Readers from any tradition (Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Protestant
of any stripe, non-denominational, inquirer) are invited to
evaluate POB against their own framework. Where a translation
decision is influenced by a theological reading — for example,
where a Greek construction is genuinely ambiguous and the English
choice leans one way or the other — that choice is documented in
the verse's `theological_decisions` block and the alternative
rendering is preserved in a footnote.

We do not pick sides on denominational distinctives (Reformed vs.
Arminian, infant vs. believer's baptism, real presence vs.
symbolic, cessationist vs. continuationist, etc.). Those questions
are for the reader and their faith community, not for the
translation.

## Translation philosophy

The People's Open Bible aims at **optimal equivalence**: the most faithful,
intelligible English representation of the source's meaning, wording patterns,
literary form, and rhetorical force. This is not an automatic midpoint between
formal and dynamic translation. Readability serves source fidelity; convention
and familiarity do not override it.

Specifically:

1. **Original-language primacy with reader-conscious wording.** Where
   long-standing English renderings obscure the source text's plain
   sense, we explain the source pressure openly. For *doulos*, the main
   text uses "servant" consistently while notes and the public audit
   trail preserve bonded-status, ownership, and total-allegiance nuance
   where it is historically or theologically salient (Rom 1:1, Phil 1:1).

2. **Translate titles; use conventional name forms.** Christological
   titles are translated to preserve meaning (*Christos* →
   "Messiah" when it functions independently as a title; *Kyrios* →
   "Lord"). In name-like constructions, use the familiar English forms
   "Jesus Christ" and "Christ Jesus." Personal names are otherwise
   transliterated by standard conventions. Thus "Jesus is the Messiah"
   retains the title, while Greek *Iēsous Christos* used as a personal-name
   construction is rendered "Jesus Christ."

3. **Preserve theological tension rather than resolve it.** Where
   the source is genuinely ambiguous on a contested interpretive
   question (e.g., *pistis Christou* — "faith in Christ" vs.
   "faithfulness of Christ"), we render one in the main text and
   preserve the alternative in a footnote, documenting the
   decision in the per-verse YAML.

4. **Consistency of key terms, or documented exception.** A given
   Greek or Hebrew word should receive a consistent English gloss
   across the translation, unless context demands variance — in
   which case the variance is documented per-verse with a
   rationale. The `consistency_lint.py` tool enforces this at
   commit time.

5. **Readable modern English, not archaic or academic.** The
   target reader is a literate 18–35-year-old English speaker.
   Vocabulary should be accessible without flattening theological
   weight. We avoid both ecclesiastical jargon ("propitiation" is
   footnoted, not required) and informality that undersells the
   text's gravity.

## Source distinctions and optimal English

Source fidelity takes priority over mere familiarity or defensibility. A
significant Greek or Hebrew wording pattern must receive an explicit comparison
with the best source-transparent English candidate, even when a prior draft
already discusses it in a footnote. Prior rationale is evidence, not a veto.
Do not infer different meanings from morphology alone or invent theology to
justify different glosses; preserve observable wording without adding claims.
A concise source-qualified or hyphenated rendering is available when ordinary
English otherwise conceals the source pattern. Record unresolved proposals for
maintainer review; do not silently certify them as unchanged or auto-publish.

**Approved scoped rendering:** John 21:15–17 uses **agape-love** for ἀγαπάω
and **phileo-love** for φιλέω, including the repeated question in verse 17.
The ἀγάπη noun's general table entry below is not a rule erasing that verb
pattern. Do not revert this approved POB/SPOB wording to generic “love”.

## Contested terms

The following terms appear frequently and carry heavy theological
weight. Our default rendering and rationale are recorded here.
Per-verse variance is documented in the individual YAML files.

| Greek / Hebrew | Default English | Alternatives considered | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Χριστός *Christos* | Messiah where independently titular; Christ in the name forms "Jesus Christ" / "Christ Jesus" | Christ, Messiah | Preserves the title's Hebraic messianic meaning while using the recognizable conventional English personal name |
| κύριος *Kyrios* | Lord | LORD, Master | Matches covenantal and NT usage |
| δοῦλος *doulos* | servant | bondservant, slave | Uses reader-facing "servant" consistently; documents bonded-status and ownership nuance in notes/audit metadata |
| πίστις *pistis* | faith | faithfulness, trust | Main text: faith; footnote alternatives where contested |
| δικαιοσύνη *dikaiosynē* | righteousness | justice | Both renderings preserved in footnotes for Pauline passages |
| ἱλαστήριον *hilastērion* | atoning sacrifice | propitiation, mercy seat | Dynamic rendering for accessibility; alternatives footnoted |
| ἀγάπη *agapē* | love | charity (archaic) | Lexical cognates in source kept |
| σάρξ *sarx* | flesh (literal) / sinful nature (metaphorical) | — | Context-dependent; per-verse documented |
| μετανοέω / μετάνοια *metanoeō / metanoia* | reorient / reorientation; toward God where the context warrants making the destination explicit | repent / repentance (traditional); reconsider / change of mind in documented exceptions | See "Reorientation terminology (2026-10-11)" below; do not homogenize regret, divine relenting, or distinct turning words |
| νήφω *nēphō* | clear-minded (most contexts); sober (where Paul explicitly runs the drunk/sober metaphor) | sober-minded | See revision notes in 1 Pet 5:8, 1 Thess 5:6 |
| יְהוָה YHWH | Yahweh | the LORD, Jehovah | Renders the divine name as a name. Where the NT quotes an OT YHWH passage using *Kyrios*, the NT verse retains "Lord" to preserve the Greek; the OT source verse uses "Yahweh". |
| אָדָם *adam* | man / humankind (context) | — | Context-dependent per usage |

## Reorientation terminology (2026-10-11)

Maintainer-approved English POB and SPOB reader wording uses **reorient /
reorientation** in place of the repent family for moral-spiritual redirection.
Use **toward God** when the context warrants making that direction explicit;
use **toward you** in direct prayer, and omit the extra destination when the
sentence already names it, supplies a departure from wrongdoing, or concerns
interpersonal reconsideration. Acts 20:21 explicitly supplies the Godward
phrase. The word *metanoia* by itself does not lexically contain "God."

This is an English editorial policy, not a claim that remorse is irrelevant or
that Greek word parts establish the full meaning. Preserve sorrow, named sins,
faith, forgiveness, and the distinction between a response and its fruit.
Keep separate turning expressions in Acts 3:19 and 26:20. Baptism's relationship
to reorientation must not be rewritten as "only symbolizes" or "causes."

**Context controls exceptions.** Retain regret, relenting, reconsideration,
change of mind, or turning back where that is the supported sense. Do not make
God reorient toward God; do not make a persecutor's demand for apostasy a call
toward God. Preserve contested interpretations in Job 42:6 and Hebrews 12:17.
Extra-canonical authors retain their own conceptual frameworks. Adapting a
historical English witness is not a new ancient-language translation, and must
be disclosed while its source transcription remains untouched.

**No invented intensifiers.** Do not add "fully," "completely," "radically,"
"truly," "wholeheartedly," or a superlative simply to strengthen reorientation.
Preserve such force only where the source supplies it. Hermas V.3.xiii.4
(reader chapter 21:4) has *holotelōs* and *ex holēs kardias*; its existing
"completely" and "from their whole heart" are not new additions.

Traditional terminology remains in alternative notes, original sources, and
historical revision records. Do not rewrite those layers to manufacture a
history of agreement. See [the application report](docs/REORIENTATION_POLICY_2026-10-11.md)
and the hash-bound plan in `config/terminology/`.

## What the translation is not

To prevent misunderstanding:

- **Not a paraphrase.** Every English rendering is tied to a
  specific source-text word or phrase, documented in the per-verse
  YAML.
- **Not a study Bible.** Footnotes document translation decisions,
  not doctrinal application or devotional commentary.
- **Not a denominational product.** The translation is
  intentionally cross-denominational. Contested readings are
  preserved in footnotes, not smoothed away.
- **Not a finalized translation.** Every verse is currently an
  AI-drafted rendering, released openly with full rationale. There
  is no formal scholarly review process at this time.
- **Not a first-century English approximation.** We aim at modern
  English that honors source-language meaning, not at archaism.

## Translating into other languages

The People's Open Bible's long-term intention is to be translated
into every major world language. Scripture belongs to the whole
church; producing POB only in English would contradict the
project's mission.

Each target language is its own translation — drafted directly
from the original-language sources (Hebrew OT, Greek NT, Swete
LXX for the deuterocanonical books) rather than from the English
POB. Translating from English would compound the distance from the
originals and inherit choices that make sense in English but not
elsewhere. Every target language deserves its own encounter with
the Hebrew and Greek.

Each language goes through **several revision passes** before it
is considered stable:

1. **AI-drafted first pass** — a frontier multilingual model
   produces the initial verse-by-verse draft with full per-verse
   provenance, following the same methodology used for English
   (DOCTRINE.md translation philosophy §§1–5, per-verse YAML
   schema, `doctrine_reference` citations where relevant).
2. **AI-reviewer revision** — a second, distinct model reads the
   draft and flags awkward phrasing, dropped nuance, or places
   where the target language's idiom has drifted from the
   source's force. Revisions are discrete commits.
3. **Native-speaker community review** — before a language is
   declared stable, speakers of that language who are also
   familiar with the biblical source languages (or who have
   access to published lexicons in that language) audit the
   text and raise issues publicly.
4. **Public issue window** — a minimum public-review period with
   open GitHub issues before any language moves from "preview"
   to "stable."

**Supported languages will be disclosed publicly based on model
performance and feasibility.** Not every language has an AI model
capable of scholarly-accurate translation yet, and not every
language has a sufficient community of native-speaking reviewers
accessible to the project. We will publish the current supported-
language list, and the ready-but-not-yet-stable list, as we reach
the capability threshold for each. Languages that do not yet meet
the bar are named as such, not silently omitted.

Every language published under this program carries the same
CC-BY 4.0 license, the same per-verse provenance, the same
auditability. There is no tier system across languages — every
supported language gets the full People's Open Bible.

context.ambiguity_review_standard: Apply the supplied DOCTRINE.md ambiguity policy: a defensible contextual rendering may be used in the main text when material alternatives and the reason for the choice are preserved in notes. A unique or uncontested interpretation is not required. Distinguish (a) an unreadable or unverified source, omitted content, invented restoration, or a construction for which no defensible English can be given, from (b) ordinary lexical, attachment, or referent ambiguity faithfully preserved in English or explained with viable alternatives. The former blocks publication; the latter does not automatically block it. A note cannot excuse unsupported wording: the proposed main rendering must itself be defensible from the supplied Greek. Clearly printed gaps must remain gaps, not be filled by invention. Never change a verdict merely to achieve acceptance.

passages.text: The deacons of the church, then, should be the bishop’s eyes, moving about with discernment and investigating the actions of each person in the church to see who is about to sin, so that, having been checked by admonition from the one who presides, that person perhaps will not carry the sin through at all. They should turn back those who desert the ranks, so that those who gather do not fail to listen to the discourses, in order that by the word of truth they may be able to clear away the discouragements that from time to time fall upon the heart from both life’s misfortunes and evil associations. For if they remain fallow for a long time, they become fuel for fire. They should also find out about those who are sick in body and bring them to the attention of the multitude that is unaware, so that its members may come forward; and they should provide what is needed according to the judgment of the one who presides. Even if they do this without his knowledge, they do not sin. The deacons, then, should take thought for these and similar matters.

lexical_decisions.chosen: should be the bishop’s eyes, moving about with discernment
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both the image of the deacons as eyes and their prudent movement throughout the community.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἑκάστου τῆς ἐκκλησίας πολυπραγμονοῦντες τὰς πράξεις τίς μέλλει ἁμαρτάνειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: investigating the actions of each person in the church to see who is about to sin
lexical_decisions.rationale: Makes τίς clearly interrogative and presents the inquiry as the purpose of examining each person’s conduct.

lexical_decisions.chosen: having been checked by admonition
lexical_decisions.rationale: Καταλαμβάνω here describes intervention reaching or arresting the person before the contemplated sin is completed.

lexical_decisions.chosen: They should turn back those who desert the ranks
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the military image of leaving one’s assigned position and the restorative force of ἐπιστρέφω.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ μὴ ἐπιλείπειν τοὺς συνερχομένους τῶν λόγων ἐπακούειν
lexical_decisions.chosen: so that those who gather do not fail to listen to the discourses
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes τοὺς συνερχομένους as the accusative subject and ἐπακούειν as the infinitival complement of ἐπιλείπειν, a defensible construction that fits the concern about continued attendance and instruction.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰς ἑκάστοτε τῇ καρδίᾳ προσπιπτούσας ἀθυμίας
lexical_decisions.chosen: the discouragements that from time to time fall upon the heart
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the source’s image of recurring discouragements falling upon the heart.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: χρόνῳ πολλῷ χερσεύσωσιν, πυρὸς ἔργον γίνονται
lexical_decisions.chosen: remain fallow for a long time, they become fuel for fire
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the movement from agricultural neglect to the image of material consumed by fire.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοὺς δὲ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα νοσοῦντας μανθανέτωσαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: They should also find out about those who are sick in body
lexical_decisions.rationale: Renders μανθάνω as ascertaining the condition of people whose illness is explicitly bodily.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται
lexical_decisions.chosen: bring them to the attention of the multitude that is unaware, so that its members may come forward
lexical_decisions.rationale: Understands the deacons as making the sick known to the congregation so that members of the collective multitude may appear or come forward; alternative referents remain possible.

source_issues.source_quote: τοῦ μὴ ἐπιλείπειν τοὺς συνερχομένους τῶν λόγων ἐπακούειν
source_issues.issue: The main rendering treats τοὺς συνερχομένους as the accusative subject of ἐπιλείπειν and takes ἐπακούειν as its complement. Other defensible attachments are possible: ἐπακούειν may describe the purpose for which people assemble, with ἐπιλείπειν meaning that they fall away or become wanting; or the deacons may be the unexpressed subject of transitive ἐπιλείπειν, yielding “so that they do not abandon those who assemble to listen.” The selected construction is contextually coherent and does not require emending the supplied Greek.

source_issues.source_quote: συνπτώσεων
source_issues.issue: The supplied edition prints the unassimilated spelling συνπτώσεων. The form is intelligible as the word conventionally normalized συμπτώσεων and does not obstruct translation.

source_issues.source_quote: ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἂν χρόνῳ πολλῷ χερσεύσωσιν, πυρὸς ἔργον γίνονται
source_issues.issue: The plural subject is not restated. The main rendering refers it to the people whose continued gathering and listening have just been discussed, which suits the image of people becoming uncultivated through neglect. A grammatical reference to the discouragements is less contextually natural but cannot be excluded solely by morphology.

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται
source_issues.issue: The rare προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν and the subject of ἐπιφαίνωνται allow more than one interpretation. The main text understands the sick as being brought to the congregation’s attention and the members of the collective multitude as then coming forward. Alternatively, the sick themselves may be the grammatical subject of “appear” or “present themselves.” The context supports the selected construction, but the Greek does not explicitly say “visit the sick.”

passages.text: The passengers, then, should remain stable, seated firmly in their own places, so that through disorder they do not cause rocking or a list to one side. The ship’s recruiting officers should remind them of the wages. The deacons should neglect none of the things entrusted to them. The elders, like sailors, should carefully prepare what each person needs. The bishop, as a watchful bow officer, should repeat only the helmsman’s words. The Messiah should be loved as Savior and helmsman, and he alone should be trusted concerning what he says. All should pray to God that they may sail with a favorable wind. Those sailing should expect every affliction, as they sail beside a great and turbulent deep—the world—at one time discouraged, persecuted, scattered, hungry, thirsty, without clothing, and distressed, and again at another time united, gathered together, and at rest, but also seasick, dizzy, and vomiting (that is, confessing offenses as though they were disease-producing bile—I mean sins arising from bitterness and the evils heaped up from disorderly desires. By confessing these, as though you had vomited them, you are relieved of the illness and receive the saving health that comes from attentive care).

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εὐσταθείτωσαν οὖν οἱ ἐπιβάται ἑδραῖοι ἐπὶ τῶν ἰδίων καθεζόμενοι τόπων
lexical_decisions.chosen: The passengers, then, should remain stable, seated firmly in their own places
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both the demand for stability and the passengers’ firm occupation of their respective places.

lexical_decisions.chosen: rocking or a list to one side
lexical_decisions.rationale: Distinguishes general shaking from an unequal inclination of the ship toward one side.

lexical_decisions.chosen: The ship’s recruiting officers should remind them of the wages
lexical_decisions.rationale: Ναυστολόγοι denotes those who enroll or recruit a ship’s company; the recipient of the reminder is implicit, while μισθοί retains the image of promised wages or rewards.

lexical_decisions.chosen: should carefully prepare what each person needs
lexical_decisions.rationale: Treats τὰ χρῄζοντα as the necessary provisions or arrangements appropriate to each person.

lexical_decisions.chosen: as a watchful bow officer
lexical_decisions.rationale: Πρωρεύς is the officer stationed toward the bow, while ἐγρηγορώς emphasizes continued watchfulness.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοῦ κυβερνήτου μόνου τοὺς λόγους ἀντιβαλλέτω
lexical_decisions.chosen: should repeat only the helmsman’s words
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes the helmsman’s words as the direct object and understands ἀντιβάλλω as giving them back or reproducing them, fitting the bishop’s subordinate role in the ship analogy.

lexical_decisions.chosen: The Messiah should be loved as Savior and helmsman
lexical_decisions.rationale: Renders the independent title χριστός as “Messiah” and preserves both adjacent designations, σωτήρ and κυβερνήτης.

lexical_decisions.chosen: seasick, dizzy, and vomiting
lexical_decisions.rationale: The author’s ensuing explanation in terms of expelling disease-producing bile strongly supports a purgative or vomiting sense for the uncommon final form.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: προσιέμενοι τὴν ἐκ τῆς ἐπιμελείας σωτήριον ὑγείαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: receive the saving health that comes from attentive care
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the medical image of accepting restorative health produced by care or treatment.

source_issues.source_quote: ὥσπερ ’ναῦται
source_issues.issue: The supplied print places a raised mark before ναῦται although ordinary elision does not account for it. The translation treats the mark as a nonlexical editorial or typographic feature without claiming that it is an OCR error.

source_issues.source_quote: ὡς πρωρεὺς ’ἐγρηγορὼς
source_issues.issue: The raised mark before ἐγρηγορὼς is not required by the apparent syntax or ordinary elision. Its typographic or editorial function is uncertain, but it does not prevent a defensible translation of the surrounding words.

source_issues.source_quote: τοῦ κυβερνήτου μόνου τοὺς λόγους ἀντιβαλλέτω
source_issues.issue: The exact action of ἀντιβαλλέτω is lexically open. The main text chooses “repeat,” taking the helmsman’s words as what the bow officer gives back or reproduces. “Answer with” or “exchange” has support from conversational usage, while “relay” would fit the nautical setting but adds an unexpressed onward recipient. The selected rendering is defensible without altering the Greek.

source_issues.source_quote: ὁ χριστὸς ὡς σωτὴρ κυβερνήτης φιλείσθω
source_issues.issue: The single ὡς introduces the adjacent nouns σωτήρ and κυβερνήτης without an expressed conjunction. The translation coordinates them in idiomatic English as “Savior and helmsman.” They may alternatively be heard as a combined designation, “Savior-helmsman,” or as “the saving helmsman.”

source_issues.source_quote: ἐνούμενοι
source_issues.issue: The supplied form has smooth breathing. The context contrasts scattering with being united and supports identification with the unity verb conventionally written ἑνόω. This is an intelligible orthographic feature, not grounds for treating the verified print as unreadable.

source_issues.source_quote: ἀπερῶντες
source_issues.issue: The form is uncommon, but its purgative sense is made intelligible by the author’s immediate explanation involving disease-producing bile and the related form ἀπεράσαντες later in the same sentence. The exact lexical formation remains uncertain, while the contextual action is defensibly rendered as vomiting.

passages.text: Nevertheless, all of you know that the bishop toils more than all of you, because each of you suffers his own affliction, whereas he suffers both his own and that of each person. Therefore, Clement, preside as a helper to each person, as far as you are able, burdened with the cares of everyone. Accordingly, in your undertaking to administer, I know that I have received a favor, not given one. But take courage and bear it nobly, knowing that when you have reached the harbor of rest, God will give you in return the greatest of good things—an inalienable reward—because you undertook the greater toil for the salvation of all. Thus, if many of the brothers hate you because of righteousness carried to the utmost, their hatred will do you no harm, but the friendship of the righteous God will benefit you greatly. Therefore, strive to shake off praise arising from injustice, but through just administration to hunt for the beneficial praise that comes from the Messiah.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πάντων ὑμῶν πλεῖον κάμνοντα τὸν ἐπίσκοπον
lexical_decisions.chosen: the bishop toils more than all of you
lexical_decisions.rationale: The accusative-infinitive construction presents the bishop as bearing greater wearisome labor than every individual hearer.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἕκαστος ὑμῶν τὴν αὐτοῦ θλίψιν πάσχει, αὐτὸς δὲ τὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν ἑκάστου
lexical_decisions.chosen: each of you suffers his own affliction, whereas he suffers both his own and that of each person
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the contrast between each member’s individual distress and the bishop’s additional burden for every member.

lexical_decisions.chosen: preside as a helper
lexical_decisions.rationale: Combines Clement’s leading position with the explicitly stated role of helping those under his care.

lexical_decisions.chosen: burdened with the cares of everyone
lexical_decisions.rationale: The passive participle portrays Clement as loaded with the collective concerns of the community.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in your undertaking to administer
lexical_decisions.rationale: Treats σέ as the accusative subject of the whole infinitival expression: Clement undertakes the administration just assigned to him. This accords with the immediate commission and does not force σέ to be the object of οἰκονομεῖν.

lexical_decisions.chosen: an inalienable reward
lexical_decisions.rationale: The adjective describes a reward that cannot be removed or taken away.

lexical_decisions.chosen: righteousness carried to the utmost
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the expression’s image of righteousness reaching its furthest extent.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸν ἐκ χριστοῦ ἐπωφελῆ θηρεύειν ἔπαινον
lexical_decisions.chosen: to hunt for the beneficial praise that comes from the Messiah
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the hunting image of θηρεύω, the advantageous character of the praise, and Χριστός as an independent title.

source_issues.source_quote: τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι χάριν οἶδα εἰληφώς, οὐ δεδωκώς
source_issues.issue: The main rendering treats σέ as the accusative subject of the entire infinitival expression, “your undertaking to administer,” while the nominative participles εἰληφώς and δεδωκώς refer to the first-person speaker, who knows himself to have received rather than given a favor. An alternative analysis makes τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν the object of ἀναδέξασθαι, with the speaker undertaking the arrangement that Clement administer. A less contextually suitable reading takes σέ as the direct object of οἰκονομεῖν, so that the speaker undertakes to administer Clement. The explicit accusative can defensibly be the embedded subject, and the immediate commission to Clement supports that choice; no emendation is required.

source_issues.source_quote: ’σωτηρίας
source_issues.issue: The supplied print places a raised mark before σωτηρίας although no ordinary elision is apparent. The mark does not affect the intelligible phrase ὑπὲρ τῆς τῶν πάντων σωτηρίας and is treated as a nonlexical editorial or typographic feature.

passages.text: But you should also understand some things on your own, because he is unable to speak openly on account of the plots. For example, if he is hostile to someone, do not wait for him to say, “Do not have dealings with this person.” Instead, prudently follow his intention, becoming enemies of those to whom he is hostile and not associating with those with whom he does not associate, so that each person, laying claim to having everyone as friends, may be saved by reconciling him and heeding his discourse. But if anyone remains a friend of those to whom he is hostile and speaks with those with whom he does not associate, that person too is one of those who want to destroy the church. For although he is with you in body, since he is not with you in purpose, he is against you—much worse than the enemies who are visibly outside, scattering those inside while maintaining seeming friendship.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἔνια δὲ καὶ ἀφ᾽ ἑαυτῶν νοεῖν ὀφείλετε
lexical_decisions.chosen: you should also understand some things on your own
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the demand that the hearers infer matters for themselves rather than waiting for an explicit public statement.

lexical_decisions.chosen: speak openly
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase refers to public or unconcealed speech, contrasted with intentions that must be inferred because of plots.

lexical_decisions.chosen: have dealings with
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb can denote engaging, associating, or contending with someone; the surrounding language of friendship and conversation supports the broad relational rendering.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀλλὰ φρονίμως ἕπεσθε αὐτοῦ τῷ βουλήματι
lexical_decisions.chosen: Instead, prudently follow his intention
lexical_decisions.rationale: The hearers are told to discern and conform to the leader’s will even when he cannot state it openly.

lexical_decisions.chosen: laying claim to having everyone as friends
lexical_decisions.rationale: The middle verb presents the person as asserting or pursuing a claim to the state expressed by the genitive infinitival phrase.

lexical_decisions.chosen: reconciling him
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves αὐτόν as the explicit direct object of the active participle rather than silently changing the construction into self-reconciliation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: heeding his discourse
lexical_decisions.rationale: The recurring singular pronouns most naturally continue to refer to the presiding leader whose intention and associations govern the paragraph.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῇ γνώμῃ μὴ ὢν μεθ᾽ ὑμῶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: since he is not with you in purpose
lexical_decisions.rationale: Contrasts bodily presence with inward judgment, intention, or allegiance.

lexical_decisions.chosen: while maintaining seeming friendship
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the characterization of the friendship as apparent rather than genuine.

source_issues.source_quote: ἵνα ἕκαστος, ἐπιδικαζόμενος τοῦ πάντας φίλους ἔχειν, αὐτὸν διαλλάττων σώζηται
source_issues.issue: The main rendering understands ἕκαστος as each person who has become isolated through hostility toward the leader, and αὐτόν as the leader: wishing to retain everyone as friends, that person reconciles the leader and is saved. This follows the paragraph’s repeated singular reference to the leader and explains the communal withdrawal as pressure toward reconciliation. Grammatically, active διαλλάττων makes αὐτόν the affected object but leaves the other party to the reconciliation unexpressed. “Winning him back” or “effecting reconciliation with him” are viable contextual formulations, while identifying αὐτόν as a different alienated person is less contextually natural. The selected construction is defensible without supplying a named referent in the text.

source_issues.source_quote: τῆς αὐτοῦ ἐπακούων ὁμιλίας
source_issues.issue: The main text takes αὐτοῦ as the presiding leader, continuing the repeated references to his intention, hostility, and associations. It could grammatically resume another referent assigned to the preceding αὐτόν, but the leader remains the most continuous and contextually relevant antecedent. The English retains the pronoun rather than replacing it with an explicit name or office.

passages.text: After saying these things, there in the midst before everyone, he laid his hands on me and entreated me to sit in his own chair. When I had sat down, he immediately said this to me: “Before all my brothers who are present with me, I ask you that, whenever I depart from the life here (as is owed to me), you write a concise account and send it to James, the Lord’s brother, reaching even as far back as your thoughts from childhood and telling how, from the beginning until now, you have traveled with me, heeding the words and deeds proclaimed by me city by city. Then, toward the end, do not hesitate also to disclose the cause of my death, as I said beforehand. For this will not grieve him greatly, since he knows that what I inevitably had to suffer I discharged devoutly. Rather, he will obtain the greatest consolation when he learns that after me no unlearned man—ignorant of life-giving words and the church’s rule and without knowledge—was entrusted with the teacher’s chair. For discourse that leads astray destroys the souls of the crowds who hear it.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: there in the midst before everyone
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both the public location in the assembly’s midst and the presence of all as witnesses.

lexical_decisions.chosen: entreated me to sit
lexical_decisions.rationale: Construes the infinitive with the following finite verb despite the printed period, yielding the natural sense of earnestly urging Clement to take the chair.

lexical_decisions.chosen: I ask you
lexical_decisions.rationale: Introduces a formal request made before the assembled brothers.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ἀναγραψάμενον
lexical_decisions.chosen: you write a concise account and send it to James, the Lord’s brother
lexical_decisions.rationale: Treats the resumed σέ as the accusative subject of διαπέμψαι and ἀναγραψάμενον. English supplies “account” and “it” from the act of writing in epitome because διαπέμπω otherwise lacks an expressed object.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μέχρι καὶ τῶν ἐκ παίδων σου λογισμῶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: reaching even as far back as your thoughts from childhood
lexical_decisions.rationale: Presents the requested record as extending to Clement’s earliest stated thoughts or reflections.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῶν κατὰ πόλιν ὑπ᾽ ἐμοῦ κηρυχθέντων λόγων τε καὶ πράξεων
lexical_decisions.chosen: the words and deeds proclaimed by me city by city
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the unusual coordination in which κηρυχθέντων grammatically characterizes both the words and the deeds.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the cause of my death
lexical_decisions.rationale: Πρόφασις can denote cause, occasion, or pretext; an account of Peter’s death supports “cause” here.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὃ πάντως ἔδει με παθεῖν εὐσεβῶς ἀπεδόμην
lexical_decisions.chosen: what I inevitably had to suffer I discharged devoutly
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the necessary suffering as an obligation that the speaker has paid or fulfilled in a devout manner.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐκ ἀμαθὴς ἀνὴρ καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς τὴν τοῦ διδάσκοντος ἐπιστεύθη καθέδραν
lexical_decisions.chosen: no unlearned man—ignorant of life-giving words and the church’s rule and without knowledge—was entrusted with the teacher’s chair
lexical_decisions.rationale: Gives the first οὐκ broad scope over the entrusting of the described kind of successor, while rendering the further explicit οὐκ εἰδώς as “without knowledge.” This yields the consolation required by the context and preserves both negations.

lexical_decisions.chosen: For discourse that leads astray
lexical_decisions.rationale: Renders πλάνος by its active force of causing hearers to wander or be deceived.

source_issues.source_quote: καθεσθῆναί με. ἐδυσώπησεν
source_issues.issue: The printed period separates the infinitive from the finite verb that most naturally governs it. The translation construes them together as “entreated me to sit.” This treats the punctuation as an editorial feature of the supplied edition, not as proof that the Greek words are corrupt.

source_issues.source_quote: συνπαρόντων
source_issues.issue: The supplied edition prints the unassimilated spelling συνπαρόντων. It is intelligible as the form conventionally normalized συμπαρόντων and does not impede translation.

source_issues.source_quote: Ἀξιῶ σε ἐπὶ πάντων μου τῶν συνπαρόντων ἀδελφῶν, ὅπως ὁπόταν τοῦ ἐνταῦθα (ὡς ἐμοὶ ὀφείλεται) ἀπαλλάξω βίου, σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ἀναγραψάμενον
source_issues.issue: The main construction takes the second σέ as a resumed accusative subject after the intervening temporal clause, with ἀναγραψάμενον agreeing with Clement and διαπέμψαι denoting his dispatch of the resulting account to James. The following section’s statement that Clement made and sent the epitome supports this role assignment. Alternatively, σέ could formally be taken as the object of διαπέμψαι, “send you,” but that would require the speaker to remain the unexpressed subject and fits the ensuing account less well. The object sent is unexpressed in Greek and is supplied in English from the writing of the epitome.

source_issues.source_quote: ἔπειτα πρὸς τῷ τέλει καὶ τὴν τοῦ θανάτου μου πρόφασιν ὡς προεῖπον δηλῶσαι μὴ ὀκνήσῃς
source_issues.issue: The main text takes the final μὴ ὀκνήσῃς directly with δηλῶσαι: after the earlier request to write and send the account, Clement is specifically told not to hesitate to disclose the cause of the death near its end. It is also possible to give “do not hesitate” wider scope over both the dispatch and the final disclosure. The selected narrower attachment follows the immediate position of δηλῶσαι and yields a defensible sequence of instructions.

source_issues.source_quote: οὐκ ἀμαθὴς ἀνὴρ καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς τὴν τοῦ διδάσκοντος ἐπιστεύθη καθέδραν
source_issues.issue: The first οὐκ can be read with broad propositional scope: it was not a man characterized as unlearned and ignorant who was entrusted with the chair. This is the main rendering and coheres with James’s resulting consolation. A strictly local reading produces “a not-unlearned man” who nevertheless is ignorant of life-giving words and the church’s rule, an awkward contrast. Another possible analysis distributes the first negation over the coordinated descriptions, yielding the positive sense that the successor was neither unlearned nor ignorant. The explicit second negation in οὐκ εἰδώς is retained as “without knowledge.” The ambiguity concerns scope, not an unreadable source.

source_issues.source_quote: κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς
source_issues.issue: The printed period interrupts the sequence of descriptions before οὐκ εἰδώς. The translation treats the participle as continuing the characterization of the man entrusted with the chair. The punctuation is preserved as a disclosed editorial feature and does not by itself establish corruption or require a conjectural reading.
